title: Shared Responsibility
prompt: Which responsibility is primarily managed by AWS? Select one correct answer.

choices.text: Physical security of AWS facilities
choices.explanation: AWS manages the physical cloud infrastructure and facilities.

choices.text: Updating the guest OS installed by the customer
choices.explanation: Updating the guest OS is the customer's responsibility.

choices.text: Configuring security groups created by the customer
choices.explanation: Customers manage service configurations.

learning.reason: Think of the boundary as AWS managing the physical infrastructure and customers managing configurations and data in the cloud.
learning.concept: Distinguish between security of the cloud and security in the cloud.

title: Regions and AZs
prompt: Select the one incorrect statement about Regions and Availability Zones.

choices.text: A Region contains multiple AZs.
choices.explanation: An AZ is an independent location within a Region.

choices.text: Deploying across multiple AZs increases resilience to a single-AZ failure.
choices.explanation: Distributing across AZs separates the scope of failures.

choices.text: An AZ is itself a geographic Region spanning the globe.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. An AZ is a location within one Region.

learning.reason: Understanding the hierarchy between Regions and AZs is the starting point for availability design.
learning.concept: A Region is a geographic unit; an AZ is an isolated location within a Region.

title: Service Roles
prompt: Select two correct statements about the combination of EC2, S3, and IAM.

choices.text: S3 is a service for storing objects.
choices.explanation: S3 is object storage.

choices.text: IAM is object storage for storing images and videos.
choices.explanation: IAM is an access control service, not a storage service.

choices.text: IAM manages permissions for users and roles.
choices.explanation: IAM handles authentication, authorization, and policies.

learning.reason: Separating storage from access control helps you combine services according to their responsibilities.
learning.concept: S3 handles data, IAM handles permissions, and EC2 handles compute.

title: Choose the 2 incorrect descriptions of core services.
prompt: Choose the 2 descriptions of core services that are incorrect.

choices.text: EC2 provides on-demand compute capacity.
choices.explanation: EC2 provides compute capacity, such as virtual servers.

choices.text: S3 is a virtual machine that is always stored in a single AZ only.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. S3 is object storage, not a virtual machine.

choices.text: IAM policies are settings that increase the capacity of stored data.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Policies define permissions.

learning.reason: For questions that ask you to choose incorrect statements, record in correct the set of incorrect choices requested by the question, rather than the choices that are factually correct.
learning.concept: correct is the set of IDs to select; it is not a list of whether each choice is true or false.

title: The role of a port
prompt: Choose one correct statement about the role of a port.

choices.text: Distinguishes destination services on the same host.
choices.explanation: A port number identifies the destination within a host.

choices.text: Converts an IP address into a DNS name.
choices.explanation: Name resolution is the role of DNS.

choices.text: Encrypts all communication.
choices.explanation: A port number alone does not provide encryption.

learning.reason: Thinking of the IP address as identifying the host and the port as identifying a service on that host helps you break down the communication path.
learning.concept: The destination IP and destination port are separate pieces of information.

title: TCP and UDP
prompt: Select the two statements about TCP and UDP that are incorrect.

choices.text: TCP is used for communications where reliability is important.
choices.explanation: TCP provides reliability through connection management, retransmission, and other mechanisms.

choices.text: UDP always guarantees delivery order and retransmission.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. UDP itself does not guarantee delivery order or retransmission.

choices.text: Port numbers alone determine the IP route from source to destination.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Routing is determined by the destination IP and route tables, among other things.

learning.reason: Consider transport-layer properties separately from network-layer routing.
learning.concept: Choosing TCP or UDP alone does not automatically determine the route or encryption.

title: DNS Records
prompt: Select 2 statements about DNS that are correct.

choices.text: A CNAME points from an alias to the canonical name.
choices.explanation: A CNAME represents an alias for a canonical name.

choices.text: An NS record identifies a zone’s name servers.
choices.explanation: NS provides information about name servers, such as delegated name servers.

choices.text: The longer the TTL, the more certainly changes take effect immediately.
choices.explanation: This is the opposite. Because the cache remains for longer, changes may take longer to take effect.

learning.reason: Distinguish the roles of name aliases, zone authority, and cache lifetime.
learning.concept: DNS is a distributed database that handles namespaces and resource records.

title: TTL
prompt: Choose the one incorrect statement about TTL.

choices.text: TTL is the amount of time a resolver caches a response.
choices.explanation: TTL is a cache duration measured in seconds.

choices.text: A short TTL makes it easier to see changes sooner.
choices.explanation: With a short TTL, more new queries are made, which can help changes take effect sooner.

choices.text: A longer TTL guarantees that the response will be new even after a change.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. With a long TTL, old responses remain cached for longer.

learning.reason: TTL determines how long a cache waits before making a new query; it does not determine whether a change is correct.
learning.concept: A short TTL helps changes take effect sooner; a long TTL reduces queries and provides stability.

title: Prefix length
prompt: Choose one correct statement about CIDR.

choices.text: In IPv4, /24 represents a block of 256 addresses.
choices.explanation: It uses 24 of the 32 bits for the prefix, leaving 2^8 addresses.

choices.text: /26 is a larger address block than /24.
choices.explanation: A /26 has a longer prefix and therefore a smaller block.

choices.text: CIDR represents the TTL of a DNS record.
choices.explanation: CIDR is a notation for an IP address range.

learning.reason: Count the bits outside the prefix to calculate the number of addresses in an IPv4 block.
learning.concept: The number of IPv4 addresses is 2^(32 − prefix length).

title: Subnets and route tables
prompt: Select the two correct statements about VPC subnets and route tables.

choices.text: Each subnet is associated with a route table.
choices.explanation: The route table associated with each subnet controls routing.

choices.text: 0.0.0.0/0 automatically represents all IPv6 addresses too.
choices.explanation: A separate route for ::/0 is required for IPv6.

choices.text: A route is represented by a destination CIDR and a target.
choices.explanation: The destination and target are the fundamentals of a route.

learning.reason: CIDR defines the destination range, and the route table defines the target for traffic sent to that range.
learning.concept: IPv4 and IPv6 default routes are defined separately.

title: Pipeline
prompt: Choose the one incorrect statement about CI/CD.

choices.text: Source is the starting point for changes.
choices.explanation: The source stage brings changes into the pipeline.

choices.text: Test is used to detect flawed changes early.
choices.explanation: The test stage can be used for quality checks before deployment.

choices.text: Deploy always sends changes to production regardless of the test results.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. The pipeline should be designed so that quality gates or approvals can stop it.

learning.reason: Automation should be designed as a safe flow that includes checks and stopping points, not just speed.
learning.concept: A pipeline moves changes through a source and multiple stages and actions.

title: Safe releases
prompt: Select the two statements that are incorrect about safe CI/CD operations.

choices.text: Run automated tests before deploying to production.
choices.explanation: This is a common quality gate for checking changes early.

choices.text: Continue production deployment even when the build has failed.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. A failed check should stop the deployment.

choices.text: Do not keep a known-good version for rollback.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. You need to ensure that recovery is possible.

learning.reason: Because this question asks you to select the incorrect statements, B and C are recorded as correct. Do not select A, because it describes a sound practice.
learning.concept: For a negatively worded question, “correct” refers to the choices to select, not to statements that are factually correct.
